title: Payee Spread and the Periodic Review Date of an Upgraded Personal Sender Account
content:
**Compliance standard for upgraded accounts.** Payee spread, for a Personal Sender Account moved up a level, reads the USD principal of the Bank Deposit payouts sent in the 6 months before the upgrade date, an entry dated on the same calendar day 6 months earlier or before it no longer counting, together with the recipients added to the account in the 12 months before the upgrade date, an addition dated on the same calendar day 12 months earlier or before it no longer counting. When that principal is 3000.00 USD or more and 2 or more recipients were added, 6 months are taken off the risk-weighted refresh interval; when that principal is 3000.00 USD or more and exactly 1 recipient was added, 3 months are taken off the risk-weighted refresh interval; otherwise nothing is taken off for payee spread.

## Truth table

| Bank Deposit principal paid out in the 6 months | Recipients added in the 12 months | Months taken off |
|---|---|---|
| 3000.00 USD or more | 2 or more | 6 |
| 3000.00 USD or more | exactly 1 | 3 |
| 3000.00 USD or more | none | 0 |
| below 3000.00 USD | any number | 0 |

## The two records read

- **Bank Deposit principal paid out** — the sum of the USD amounts of the payout sent entries in the ledgers of the customer's Bank Deposit transfers, dated inside the 6 months. Cash Pickup and Mobile Wallet payouts are not part of it.
- **Recipients added** — the recipient added entries on the account history, dated inside the 12 months.

## Hypothetical cases

1. Bank Deposit payouts of 1800.00 and 1200.00 USD in the 6 months (3000.00 in total) and 3 recipients added in the 12 months: 6 months taken off.
2. Bank Deposit payouts totalling 2999.99 USD and 5 recipients added: nothing taken off, because the principal is below 3000.00 USD.
3. Bank Deposit payouts totalling 4500.00 USD and 1 recipient added: 3 months taken off.
